cji_quote_sources.headline: CJI Surya Kant sparks row by calling activists, media 'cockroaches'
cji_quote_sources.wording_as_printed: "...There are youngsters like cockroaches, who don't get any employment and don't have any place in profession. Some of them become media, some of them become social media, some of them become RTI activists, some of them become other activists, and they start attacking everyone..."
cji_quote_sources.notes: Closest match to the client text. Only difference: 'in profession' where client has 'in the profession'. Printed as an excerpt with leading/trailing ellipses and attributed to LiveLaw. Text fetched and extracted directly from the page HTML.

cji_quote_sources.headline: Unemployed Youngsters Who're Like Cockroaches Become Activists & Start Attacking Every System: CJI Surya Kant
cji_quote_sources.wording_as_printed: "There are youngsters like cockroaches, who don't get any employment and don't have any place in profession." (this sentence only; rest of the quote is behind the paywall)

client_text: There are youngsters like cockroaches, who don't get any employment and don't have any place in the profession. Some of them become media, some of them become social media, some of them become RTI activists, some of them become other activists, and they start attacking everyone.

cji_clarification_sources.headline: Section Of Media Misquoted Me, Criticised Only Those Who Join Professions With Fake Degrees: CJI Surya Kant Clarifies Remarks On Youth
cji_clarification_sources.verbatim: “I am pained to read how a section of the media has misquoted my oral observations made during the hearing of a frivolous case yesterday. What I had specifically criticised were those who have entered professions like the Bar (legal profession) with the aid of fake and bogus degrees. Similar persons have sneaked into the media, social media, and other noble professions as well, and hence, they are like parasites,” ... “It is totally baseless to suggest that I criticised the youth of our nation. Not only am I proud of our present and future human resource, but every youth of India inspires me.”
cji_clarification_sources.notes: Extracted directly from page HTML (not a summary). Statement was issued on Saturday 16 May. Note he still uses the word 'parasites' in the clarification; and does not repeat 'cockroaches'.

cji_clarification_sources.headline: CJI Surya Kant says media misquoted 'cockroaches' remark; criticism was against fake degree holders, not unemployed youth
cji_clarification_sources.verbatim: (paraphrase only in what I read: 'media misquoted his oral observations which were made during hearing of a frivolous case')
cji_clarification_sources.notes: Also Bar and Bench exclusive interview 'CJI Surya Kant clarifies cockroach remark, calls for protocol on reporting oral court observations' https://www.barandbench.com/news/litigation/exclusive-cji-surya-kant-clarifies-cockroach-remark-calls-for-protocol-on-reporting-oral-court-observations (surfaced in search; not opened). Search summary says he later said 'fake degrees' meant unrecognised degrees (July 2026) - unverified.

quotes.author: M. K. Gandhi
quotes.year: 1909 (Gujarati original, Indian Opinion); English translation by Gandhi, 1910
quotes.work: Hind Swaraj / Indian Home Rule, ch. XVII 'Passive Resistance'
quotes.english_text: Passive resistance is a method of securing rights by personal suffering; it is the reverse of resistance by arms.
quotes.translator: M. K. Gandhi himself (1910 English edition)
quotes.source_note: Project Gutenberg #40461, 'Indian Home Rule' (Ganesh & Co., Madras, 5th edition). Text extracted directly from page HTML.
quotes.notes: Gujarati original NOT retrieved, so the original-script requirement is unmet; the English text is Gandhi's own translation of his Gujarati. Spoken by 'Editor' in the dialogue. Gandhi d.1948: public domain in India.

quotes.author: B. R. Ambedkar
quotes.year: 1936 (undelivered address for Jat-Pat-Todak Mandal, Lahore; published May 1936)
quotes.work: Annihilation of Caste, section 20 in the Columbia/CCNMTL edition
quotes.original_text: Political tyranny is nothing compared to social tyranny, and a reformer who defies society is a much more courageous man than a politician who defies the government.
quotes.source_note: Columbia CCNMTL web edition, paragraph [6] of section 20; extracted directly from page HTML. 31 words.
quotes.notes: Other editions differ in small ways (e.g. 'the social tyranny', 'Government' capitalised). If printing, check against the MEA/Govt of Maharashtra Writings & Speeches vol. 1 (https://www.mea.gov.in/images/CPV/Volume1.pdf) or the Anand annotated edition. Ambedkar d.1956: public domain in India.

quotes.author: Bhagat Singh (HSRA notice; primarily written by him, thrown in Central Assembly with Batukeshwar Dutt)
quotes.original_text: It takes a loud voice to make the deaf hear
quotes.source_note: Marxists Internet Archive transcription from shahidbhagatsingh.org; opening line of the notice, extracted directly from page HTML. Full sentence continues: 'with these immortal words uttered on a similar occasion by Valiant, a French anarchist martyr, do we strongly justify this action of ours.'
quotes.notes: The line is a quotation by Bhagat Singh of French anarchist Auguste Vaillant (spelt 'Valiant' on the transcription); credit it as 'Bhagat Singh quoting Vaillant', not as his own aphorism. Some outlets print 'loud noise' not 'loud voice'. Do NOT use the widely circulated 'They may kill me but they cannot kill my ideas' (unsourced).

quotes.author: Lala Lajpat Rai
quotes.work: Public meeting speech after lathi charge
quotes.original_text: I declare that the blows struck at me today will be the last nails in the coffin of British rule in India.
quotes.source_note: Britannica biography is a general source; it gives a DIFFERENT phrasing ('Every blow aimed at me is a nail in the coffin of British imperialism' per search summary). The quoted text is the most common version, appearing in an anti-Simon-Commission profile via search; no primary source found.
quotes.notes: WEAK candidate: wording varies across sources (The Tribune: 'Every blow on my body will prove to be the last nail in the coffin of British rule in India'). No 1928 newspaper or Collected Works citation found. Recommend swapping for Savitribai Phule or another Gandhi/Ambedkar line if Vali wants a clean source. I did not verify the Britannica page text myself.

quotes.author: Faiz Ahmad Faiz
quotes.nationality: Pakistani (b. Sialkot 1911, d. Lahore 1984), Urdu; widely read in India
quotes.year: not verified; Rekhta cites the book Nuskha Hai Wafa, p. 81
quotes.original_text:
بول کہ لب آزاد ہیں تیرے
بول زباں اب تک تیری ہے
quotes.roman: bol ki lab āzād haiñ tere / bol zabāñ ab tak terī hai
quotes.english_text: Speak, your lips are free, speak, your tongue is still yours
quotes.translator: Not named on Rekhta (page prints an unattributed English rendering: 'Speak, your lips are free, speak, your tongue is still yours, your slim body is yours alone, speak, this life is yours, still yours.')
quotes.source_note: Rekhta nazm page; Urdu script read from ?lang=ur version of the page, Roman and English from the default version. 13 words.
quotes.notes: Rekhta's English is unattributed; if a named translator is needed, V. G. Kiernan's 'Poems by Faiz' (1971) is the standard English edition but I did NOT verify that it contains 'Bol', so do not credit it. Copyright: Faiz d.1984, still in copyright in India; short quote use needs fair-dealing judgement or permission.

quotes.author: Habib Jalib
quotes.year: 1962 (per Wikipedia and Express Tribune via search; written against Ayub Khan's constitution)
quotes.original_text:
ایسے دستور کو صبح بے نور کو
میں نہیں مانتا میں نہیں جانتا
quotes.roman: aise dastūr ko sub.h-e-be-nūr ko / maiñ nahīñ māntā maiñ nahīñ jāntā
quotes.english_text: That kind of system, like dawn without light, I refuse to acknowledge, I refuse to accept
quotes.translator: None named. This wording is the unattributed translation in the English Wikipedia 'Habib Jalib' article (CC BY-SA); Rekhta has no English for this nazm. Treat as supplied/unattributed.
quotes.source_note: Rekhta nazm page (Urdu read from ?lang=ur version). Roman from Wikipedia table. 14 words. Translation from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habib_Jalib
quotes.notes: The famous refrain is 'main nahin maanta, main nahin jaanta'. Rekhta lists no book in what I extracted. Rekhta line 3 of the last stanza reads 'چارہ گر دردمندوں کے بنتے ہو کیوں' (Wikipedia version differs slightly); the lines I chose are identical on both. Jalib d.1993, in copyright. Consider an own translation: 'Such a constitution, a dawn without light: I do not accept it, I do not acknowledge it.' (ours, unverified by any translator).

quotes.author: Dushyant Kumar
quotes.year: not verified; usually dated 1975 (Saaye Mein Dhoop), but Rekhta lists the book as 'Hindustani Gazlen' and gives no year
quotes.work: Ghazal 'ho ga.ī hai piir parvat sī pighalnī chāhiye'
quotes.original_text:
सिर्फ़ हंगामा खड़ा करना मिरा मक़्सद नहीं
मेरी कोशिश है कि ये सूरत बदलनी चाहिए
quotes.english_text: My aim is not merely to raise a commotion; my effort is that this state of things must change.
quotes.translator: OURS (no published translation with a named translator found)
quotes.source_note: Rekhta Hindi ghazal page, Devanagari from ?lang=hi version. Rekhta prints 'मिरा'; some print editions use 'मेरा'. 22 words.
quotes.notes: Alternative shorter, better-known couplet from the same ghazal: 'हो गई है पीर पर्वत सी पिघलनी चाहिए / इस हिमालय से कोई गंगा निकलनी चाहिए'. Dushyant d.1975: Indian copyright runs life+60, so still protected until 2036.

quotes.author: Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar'
quotes.year: not verified; I believe ~1950 (poem titled 'Janatantra ka Janm') but no source I opened states it. Kavita Kosh page lists no collection
quotes.work: 'सिंहासन खाली करो कि जनता आती है' (also circulated as 'जनतन्त्र का जन्म')
quotes.original_text:
दो राह, समय के रथ का घर्घर-नाद सुनो,
सिंहासन खाली करो कि जनता आती है ।
quotes.english_text: Make way, hear the rumble of the chariot of time; vacate the throne, for the people are coming.
quotes.translator: OURS (the phrase 'Vacate the throne, for the people are coming' is the common English rendering, e.g. in Wikipedia's Dinkar article, but no translator is named)
quotes.source_note: Kavita Kosh; text copied from page HTML (refrain appears at line 4 of stanza 1 and repeats). 14 words.
quotes.notes: Also used by JP Narayan in the 1974-75 movement and the Ramlila Maidan 1975 rally (The Leaflet article, not opened). Dinkar d.1974; Indian copyright runs till 2035, so not public domain.

summary_notes: Quotes: 4 activists (Gandhi, Ambedkar, Bhagat Singh, Lajpat Rai) and 4 poets (Faiz, Jalib, Dushyant Kumar, Dinkar). Poems are in copyright (not PD in India); Faiz and Jalib are Pakistani.
